title: A early look at my Half Life PS1 port
author: izzy88izzy

comments.author: MAG1LIVE
comments.body: Super cool project? Could you share a bit more about how you've cooked with AI?

comments.author: FrigoCoder
comments.body: There was a texture mapping algorithm that provided exact texture coordinates without division, if I remember correctly it used some second order increments to calculate u, v coordinates. It provided correct perspective unlike affine mapping, but it was discovered too late once hardware acceleration was already widespread. You might want to look it up, and use it in your engine.

replies.author: izzy88izzy
replies.body: Hi! Are you referring to Barenbrug et al.’s midpoint-based division-free perspective-correct renderer from Graphics Hardware 2000? If that's the case it looks excellent for a software or custom-hardware rasterizer, but the PS1 GPU’s texture interpolation is fixed-function affine, so on real hardware we would still have to approximate it through subdivision.

replies.author: FrigoCoder
replies.body:
That might have been the algorithm, seems like it matches what little I remember. The ratio of polynomials and the multiple increment and addition steps seem familiar.

I don't remember exactly sorry, it was like 20 years ago on a random website in a few paragraphs. The only reason I still have vague memories is because I have also encountered this issue. I have implemented affine mapping in Turbo Pascal asm blocks, and I wanted perspective-correct texture mapping without the *enormous* cost.

I am not familiar with the PS1 at all though, so I can not comment on that one. I vaguely remember I had ideas for polygon subdivision, not only for texture mapping but also for phong lighting that was also a huge issue back then. You might try subdividing lines instead of polygons if possible, so that way you get more precise control over affine mapping.
